Subject: Deployment rights & custody-proof pathway for Private/VPC addendum

Thanks again for walking through the Private deployment request this week. Per our call, I attached a candidate set of MSA + Order Form redlines that aim to address MedTech's evidence/escrow concerns while keeping the operational burden reasonable for both sides (attached: Redwood-MSA-redlines-v3.docx).

High level proposal: instead of a traditional source-code escrow, Redwood can offer a constrained "custody & evidence" pathway for Private/VPC customers that includes:
- Encrypted 90-day VM snapshot export (customer-initiated; redacted secrets)
- Quarterly evidence packages (logs, attestation) produced by Redwood's Compliance team
- Key custody options: customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed key wrapping; proof of key handling documented in the package

Questions for you:
1) Is MedTech ok with a snapshot/attestation approach (versus an escrow deposit)?
2) If not, can you outline the minimum obligations an escrow operator would need to meet (SLA, access windows, indemnity expectations)?

Next steps: if snapshot+attestation is acceptable, legal can try to fold the language into the MSA addendum and an Order Form clause. Laura / Marissa — can you review the attached redlines and flag any non-starters before I send to Anita's legal?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher

Thanks, Sean — useful framing. A few items from our side: 

1) Snapshot approach: MedTech is open to considering a snapshot + attestation model but we need clarity on redaction and access controls. Will snapshots include any PII or customer data by default? We need guaranteed redaction steps and a clear chain-of-custody log.

2) Audit/Access: We want the ability for an independent 3rd-party to perform a for-cause review in the event of provider insolvency or persistent breach. Can that be scoped to a "for-cause" clause rather than ongoing 3rd-party escrow audits?

3) Notice windows: any on-site or image access should have a minimum 48-72 hour notice for scheduling unless it is an emergency (security incident).

On timing: our procurement team would like to see the redlines and a final Order Form to confirm PO and billing terms. Sending a short summary to Legal now; they may request additional contractual language around data retention and destruction certificates.

Anita — appreciate the quick review and practical asks. A few internal notes from Legal/Contracts: 

- Redaction: snapshots will be generated by Redwood's automated export tooling; by default, we exclude any token-level user content flagged as sensitive and we provide a metadata-only export for indexes. We can add a contract clause that snapshots will be "redacted to industry standard" and include a manifest describing data classes included/excluded.

- 3rd-party review: we can accept "for-cause" independent reviews, with two guardrails: (1) engagement limited to validation of continuity-of-service and responsiveness (not ongoing access to customer PII), and (2) engagement scoped to a single 72-hour review window unless additional cause is demonstrated.

- Notice period: we propose 72 hours for scheduled access and immediate access for security incidents with post-event reporting.

I've attached an internal note summarizing acceptable compromise language (attached: Redwood-evidence-playbook-notes.pdf). Marissa, I'm tagging you for any additional enterprise/legal redlines that should land in the MSA addendum.

Subject: Re: Deployment rights & custody-proof pathway for Private/VPC addendum

Thanks all — reviewing now. High-level position from Enterprise Legal: we can accept the snapshot + attestation path with these required contract elements: 

1) Escrow-equivalent clause: Redwood will provide encrypted VM image and an evidence package on customer request under the following conditions: customer to certify cause; limited to one for-cause production extraction per 12-month period without additional cause.
2) Evidence package contents: manifest of exports, chain-of-custody log, cryptographic hash of images, KMS key identifier and wrapping metadata; do not include raw customer PII unless explicitly requested and approved by Redwood Legal.
3) Key custody: offer two options in the Order Form — (A) customer-managed KMS (recommended) or (B) Redwood-managed KMS with HSM and key-wrapping logs available in the evidence package.
4) Liability & access: narrow the 3rd-party review scope to continuity/custody validation; no data exfiltration rights; Redwood must be given 72 hours notice for scheduled reviews.

I've prepared redline suggestions to the MSA addendum and the Order Form that implement the above; please see the tracked changes in the attached doc. If MedTech accepts, legal can provide the DocuSign-ready Order Form (I will include the two KMS options as checkboxes).

Marissa Cole
